name: HBA1C (GLYCATED HEMOGLOBIN)
description: HbA1c measures the percentage of glycated hemoglobin in red blood cells, reflecting average blood glucose levels over the past 2-3 months. This test is essential for diabetes diagnosis, monitoring long-term glycemic control, and assessing diabetes management effectiveness. The test uses high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) for accurate quantification.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Bio-Rad Variant, Tosoh G8, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) is the gold standard for assessing long-term glycemic control in diabetes mellitus. The test measures the percentage of hemoglobin that has glucose attached, reflecting average blood glucose over the previous 8-12 weeks (red blood cell lifespan). HPLC is the reference method for HbA1c measurement, providing excellent precision and accuracy. Normal HbA1c is <5.7%, prediabetes is 5.7-6.4%, and diabetes is ≥6.5%. For diabetics, target HbA1c is <7.0% (or <8.0% in some cases). The test is unaffected by short-term factors like meals, stress, or acute illness, making it ideal for monitoring. Factors affecting results include hemoglobinopathies, anemia, and certain medications. Estimated Average Glucose (eAG) can be calculated from HbA1c using the formula: eAG = (28.7 × HbA1c) - 46.7. Regular HbA1c testing (every 3-6 months) is essential for diabetes management and reducing complications.
